description: Stage 2 of the 3-file pipeline (progress.json -> review.json -> plans.json). An entry lands here ONLY when its progress.json score reached 100 with zero tbi/tbd/warnings. Workflow for ANY agent picking this up, no prior context needed: (1) pick one entry with review_status='pending_review'; (2) re-run the exact command(s) named in its 'evidence' field, do not trust the text -- run it again; (3) if the re-run output matches the evidence claim exactly, set review_status='passed', set 'review_verified_on' to today, leave it here permanently; (4) if the re-run output does NOT match (test now fails, file now missing, claim no longer true), do NOT edit this file's score -- instead: delete the entry from review.json, and add/restore it to progress.json's entries[] with score reset below 100, status='open', and a new warning describing exactly what the re-run found wrong. progress.json is the single place an open issue lives; review.json never holds an open issue. Never mark review_status='passed' without actually re-running the evidence command in this same turn.

entries.purpose: Étude notebook: local omission oddball paradigm (expected-stimulus-slot vs silent-omission-slot). Real, executable, no longer a placeholder.
warnings: jaxfne.omission_oddball_paradigm's ParadigmCondition events include trial_start/post_stimulus/post_omission timing markers, not just the real stimulus -- stimulus_schedule()'s drive heuristic (is_drive = not is_omission and onset_ms is not None) makes those marker events ALSO inject default drive amplitude, not just the labeled stimulus/omission event. Confirmed by direct inspection of jaxfne/core.py::stimulus_schedule, documented in the notebook markdown. Does not corrupt this étude's expected-vs-omitted contrast (both conditions share the same marker events, so the confound cancels in the paired subtraction) but would matter for any future paradigm reusing these conditions differently.
entries.evidence: Built via nbformat using jaxfne.omission_oddball_paradigm directly (ParadigmCondition passed straight to simulate(paradigm=...), no hand-built StimulusSchedule needed -- verified Model._resolve_stimulus_schedule natively accepts ParadigmCondition). Executed end-to-end via nbclient.NotebookClient (0 cell errors), normalized via nbformat.validator.normalize. Real results: expected=14.93+-0.14 Hz, omitted=10.00+-0.00 Hz (omitted trials are perfectly flat since no real stimulus varies them), local omission mismatch = +4.93 Hz -- a real, honest, undersold-not-oversold diagnostic. scripts/audit_notebook_grammar.py --check -> pass:true, all 5 sections present. python3 -m pytest "tests/test_notebook_execution_suite.py::test_release_notebook_executes_cleanly[etudes/jaxfne_etude_no_11_omission_local.ipynb]" -v -> 1 passed. Removed from PLACEHOLDER_NOTEBOOKS in tests/test_notebook_execution_suite.py.

entries.purpose: Étude notebook: continuous omission oddball (COOP) -- a rhythmic 6 Hz pulse train with randomly omitted pulses, run as one continuous simulation per trial. Real, executable, no longer a placeholder.
entries.evidence: Built via nbformat using jaxfne.coop_omission_oddball_paradigm directly (its omitted-pulse events set metadata={"drive_amplitude": 0.0} explicitly -- genuinely silent, unlike omission_oddball_paradigm's marker-event gap documented as F-022). Executed end-to-end via nbclient.NotebookClient (0 cell errors, ~90s for 8 continuous 2s trials at N=200), normalized via nbformat.validator.normalize. Real results: standard pulses n=62 rate=13.69+-3.80 Hz, omitted pulses n=18 rate=8.53+-1.72 Hz, global omission mismatch = +5.15 Hz -- comparable magnitude to Étude 11's local omission mismatch (+4.93 Hz), as expected for a structurally similar contrast. scripts/audit_notebook_grammar.py --check -> pass:true, all 5 sections present. python3 -m pytest "tests/test_notebook_execution_suite.py::test_release_notebook_executes_cleanly[etudes/jaxfne_etude_no_12_omission_global_coop.ipynb]" -v -> 1 passed. entries.purpose: serialize_optimization_manifest converts an optimizer state object (dataclass or NamedTuple) and a hyperparams dict into a JSON-safe dict, handling JAX/NumPy array-to-list conversion and skipping callables.
warnings: hasattr(state, "__dict__") branch will match frozen dataclasses (frozen only blocks __setattr__, not __dict__ access) but NOT NamedTuple-based states like GSGDState in gsgd.py -- NamedTuple lacks __dict__, so it falls through to the hasattr(state,"_asdict") branch first (checked first in the if/elif chain) -- verified correctly ordered by a real test (test_frozen_dataclass_state_uses_dict_path_not_asdict, test_namedtuple_state_uses_asdict_path), not just by reading source.
entries.evidence: Built tests/test_optim_manifests.py (new, 9 tests) closing the confirmed zero-coverage gap: None state, NamedTuple state (GSGDState), plain dataclass state, frozen dataclass state (confirms the _asdict/__dict__ branch ordering is correct, not just plausible), no-dict-or-asdict fallback, JAX array state-field -> list conversion, hyperparams JAX-array/int/callable-skip handling, full manifest JSON-serializability round-trip, and an unrepresentable-object fallback-to-str path. python3 -m pytest tests/test_optim_manifests.py -v -> 9 passed.

entries.purpose: Owns the public optimizer-spec grammar (OptimizerSpec, AGSDROptimizerSpec, gsdr()/agsdr()/random_search()/optax_adam()/optax_sgd()/gsgd() constructors), the JAX-native AGSDR candidate-proposal kernel (_agsdr_candidates_from_noise, jit+vmap-friendly), the differentiable quadratic-loss helper, the full multi-parameter AGSDR optimization loop (_run_agsdr_optimization_loop), Optax-compatible GradientTransformation wrappers for SDR/GSDR/AGSDR (sdr_transform/gsdr_transform/agsdr_transform), and the two-level matrix-AGSDR+Adam tuning entry point (_tune_matrix_agsdr_optax).
warnings: Defines a second, parallel set of _TransformSDRState/_TransformGSDRState/_TransformAGSDRState classes with the same bare field layout as base.py's BaseSDRState-derived SDRState/GSDRState/AGSDRState, deliberately renamed with an underscore prefix to avoid a name collision -- the in-file comment (lines 802-813) explains this is intentional, but it means the package has two independently-evolving copies of near-identical state dataclasses (one inert/pass-through in sdr.py/gsdr.py/agsdr.py, one actually wired up with EMA variance + checkpoint/deselection logic here) that could drift apart silently

_inner_loss_fn truncates simulation duration to 50ms for the inner-loop surrogate gradient regardless of the real run's duration_ms -- reasonable as a speed optimization but undocumented as a parameter (hardcoded magic number 50.0)

Duplicate _TransformSDRState/_TransformGSDRState/_TransformAGSDRState (vs base.py's SDRState/GSDRState/AGSDRState) -- FIXED-decision-documented, not fixed: in-file comment explains this is intentional to avoid a name collision, but the drift risk itself is real and not addressed this pass (out of scope -- a real design decision about state-class unification, not a mechanical fix).

entries.purpose: End-to-end Jaxley emitter bridge tests: clip-compat shim, real jaxley HH channel integration, jaxley_to_signals converter, homeostatic controller, laminar LFP/CSD from HH current.
entries.evidence: FIXED a real pre-existing latent test-order dependency bug (found while validating pytest-xdist parallel-safety, not otherwise visible under normal serial execution): only test_clip_compat_shim_lets_hh_integrate() called bridges._install_jax_clip_compat() (the shim restoring jnp.clip a_min=/a_max= kwargs that jaxley<=0.13 needs on current JAX) -- every other test in the file implicitly relied on that test having already run first IN THE SAME PROCESS. Confirmed by direct isolation: test_jaxley_to_signals_carries_positions_and_layout raised a raw jaxley/JAX TypeError when run alone (fresh process, shim never installed), but passed when run after the shim-installing test. This broke under pytest-xdist load-balanced scheduling (worker processes have independent global state) -- 11/20 notebook+jaxley test failures observed in one parallel run, traced to this exact cause. FIX: added an autouse fixture (_ensure_jax_clip_compat_shim) calling the idempotent installer before every test in the file, removing the order dependency entirely. Verified: forward order (9 passed), reverse order (9 passed), and a clean full-suite pytest -n auto run (2795 passed, 0 failed, 37m45s vs ~65min serial -- confirms both the fix and that pytest-xdist is now safe for the whole suite).
